items.title: Motivation as the Engine of ESL Success: Exploring Economic, Social, and Educational Determinants of Language Learning
items.abstract: Motivation represents one of the most influential factors affecting success in learning English as a second language (ESL). Although English proficiency is increasingly associated with academic achievement, professional advancement, and global mobility, students' willingness to engage in language learning is shaped by a complex interaction of economic, psychological, pedagogical, and sociocultural influences. Guided by Self-Determination Theory and the L2 Motivational Self System, this paper examines the major factors affecting student motivation in ESL learning. The discussion is organised around four interconnected dimensions: economic and instrumental motivations, academic self-efficacy and personal growth, pedagogical environments and motivational engagement, and cultural curiosity and media exposure. The analysis suggests that students are strongly motivated by career aspirations, financial stability, academic achievement, and communicative competence. At the same time, self-confidence, reduced communication anxiety, supportive learning environments, and exposure to authentic English-language media contribute significantly to sustained motivation. The paper further argues that teacher attitudes, innovative pedagogical practices, and opportunities for meaningful communication play a central role in transforming external motivation into internal commitment to language learning. Motivation is therefore conceptualised as a dynamic process shaped by personal aspirations and environmental influences rather than a fixed individual characteristic. Future research should investigate the role of artificial intelligence-assisted learning, digital motivation, multilingual identity, and long-term motivational development among ESL learners.

items.title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
items.abstract: Many scientific phenomena are best understood as outcomes of underlying optimization problems, yet automated scientific discovery has largely focused on recovering equations that describe observed input-output patterns. We introduce OptScientist, a novel automated framework for discovering compact symbolic optimization laws directly from data. OptScientist comprises (i) a model that infers symbolic optimization problems by first learning to represent data as an optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form, and (ii) an LLM agentic system embedding the model in a discovery process that integrates theoretical priors from scientific literature, discovers candidate laws, abstracts their underlying mechanisms, and suggests new data to collect. We first evaluate OptScientist on OptFeynman, a novel benchmark of 99 physics-derived optimization problems, where OptScientist recovers ground-truth laws for over 80% of the problems and remains robust to noisy contextual information, while substantially outperforming machine-learning, symbolic, and LLM-based model-discovery baselines. On human risky choice and central-bank monetary policy, OptScientist discovers compact symbolic optimization laws that achieve held-out predictive performance competitive with leading baselines, while using few parameters and substantially fewer tokens than LLM baselines. Overall, OptScientist extends automated scientific discovery to uncovering optimization laws that generate observed phenomena, enabling automated theory building across the physical, biological, behavioral, and social sciences.

items.title: Pengembangan Kreativitas Digital Siswa SMA 1 Sedayu melalui Pelatihan Prompt Engineering Berbasis Framework Role-Task-Context
items.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed learning and working paradigms, shifting the primary challenge from merely seeking information to the ability to formulate precise instructions (prompting). Despite high technology access in Senior High Schools (SMA), its utilization remains largely superficial. This research aims to enhance students' AI literacy skills—encompassing conceptual understanding, ethical awareness, and information verification—through structured prompt engineering training. The study employed a quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design involving 31 students at SMA 1 Sedayu, Bantul, Yogyakarta. The intervention was delivered through training based on the Role–Task–Context (RTC) framework and hands-on practice using mobile devices. Data analysis included normality tests (Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnov), Spearman correlation, and paired samples t-tests. The results indicated a significant increase in mean scores, rising from 57.10 in the pre-test to 89.68 in the post-test. Statistically, |t-Stat| (18.16) > t-Critical (2.04) with a significance value of (p < 0.05), leading to the acceptance of the alternative hypothesis (H_1). A strong Pearson correlation (0.759) demonstrated students' consistency in adopting new techniques. The training successfully transitioned students from passive technology consumers to proactive information managers. In conclusion, integrating prompt engineering as a life skill can transform students' digital behavior from mere entertainment into sophisticated productivity tools, while simultaneously strengthening digital literacy in the digital creative economy era.

items.title: Physicians’ prompting strategies for Generative Artificial Intelligence in clinical decision-making: a scoping review protocol
items.abstract: Clinical reasoning is one of the pillars of medical practice and, more recently, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has emerged as a tool to support clinical practice and decision-making. However, the incorporation of GenAI into clinical practice depends on multiple factors, including how physicians interact with these tools through user-generated prompts. This scoping review aims to map the available evidence on prompting strategies used by physicians when interacting with GenAI tools to support clinical decision-making across all levels of medical care. We will search on MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, Cochrane, Web of Science, LILACS (via BVS), Google Scholar and ProQuest. The main concept of this review is prompting strategies, defined defined as the ways in which participants structure prompts to interact with GenAI tools in the context of supporting clinical reasoning and clinical decision-making. We plan to describe the countries where the studies were conducted, GenAI tools used, and participants' professional or training level, including general practitioners, medical residents, and specialists. We will also report the prompting strategies used, prompt elements, previous user training, and the clinical questions addressed using GenAI, categorized into the following domains: basic science, risk factors or prognosis, diagnosis, treatment, communication, medical ethics, and others. The expected outcome of this review is a comprehensive mapping of how physicians interact with GenAI through prompting in clinical reasoning and decision-making, identifying the prompting strategies and prompt elements currently used, as well as gaps in the existing evidence. These findings may inform future research on physician–GenAI interaction and the development and evaluation of prompting approaches for clinical decision support.

items.title: Pre-service teachers’ AI literacy: An exploratory study of predecessor literacies and personal characteristics predictors
items.abstract: Literacy is embedded in social practices that adopt socially constructed technologies. In the 20th century, the invention of the computer facilitated information literacy and computational thinking. Media literacy emerged alongside the development of media. In the 21st century, the accessibility of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered chatbots using conversational language has expanded significantly, creating a need for their integration in education. AI literacy is being studied within frameworks similar to those of its predecessors, requiring conceptualization and differentiation from related literacy concepts. As of 2025, teacher education regarding AI literacy has been identified as an under-researched area. This article examines AI literacy through the lens of pre-service teachers’ literacy competencies that will shape the literacy practices of future generations. During their own schooling, the current generation of prospective teachers encountered information, digital, and media literacy, as well as computational thinking; these are analyzed here as predictors of AI literacy, measured using the scale for the assessment of non-experts’ artificial intelligence literacy (SNAIL) instrument. Personality traits and mindset are also investigated as predictors of the prospective teachers’ professional competence. The study was conducted in 2024/25 with a sample of pre-service teachers. The research questions are: What is the structure of AI literacy in the sample? To what extent can AI literacy be predicted by components of information literacy? How much of AI literacy can be explained by various established technology-related literacies? To what extent do personality and mindset contribute to predicting AI literacy? The findings confirmed a two-factor solution for SNAIL, comprising technical understanding and critical application. Student perception of information literacy skills proved accurate in predicting the critical application of AI. In addition to information literacy, predictors included the media production subscale of media literacy and mindset. Technical understanding of AI was predicted by the media production subscale, the computational thinking subscales algorithmic thinking and cooperativity, and the personality trait of agreeableness. Establishing AI literacy as an essential teacher competency requires thorough research into AI’s educational impacts and strict alignment with pedagogical goals. Navigating the ethical and moral dimensions of AI usage provides the necessary foundation for this literacy. Consequently, training programs can intentionally foster AI competence by merging specialized literacy modules with algorithmic thinking, media production, and growth-mindset interventions.

items.title: Prompt Literacy as a Core Workplace Competency: Development of the Prompt Literacy Index (PLI-20) for Non-Technical Professionals
items.abstract: Organizations are adopting generative artificial intelligence faster than their employees can use it well. Training investment targets tools rather than the human skill that determines output quality. This article defines prompt literacy as a distinct, measurable workplace competency: the ability of a worker to instruct, contextualize, verify, refine, and ethically govern the output of a generative AI system during ordinary job tasks. Drawing on digital literacy theory, AI literacy research, and recent evidence on prompting behavior, the article develops a five-dimension conceptual framework covering task framing, context supply, output verification, iterative refinement, and ethical use. Following established scale development procedures, a 40-item pool was generated from peer-reviewed literature published between 2004 and 2025 and reduced through a structured content-validity design to the 20-item Prompt Literacy Index (PLI-20). The full instrument is presented, together with a registered validation protocol specifying the sample, exploratory factor analysis, and reliability criteria for the planned pilot study with non-technical professionals. The article contributes the first profession-agnostic framework and instrument for measuring applied prompting skill outside technical roles, shifting the unit of analysis in workplace AI research from the tool to the worker. Implications for workforce development, training design, and future confirmatory validation are discussed. Keywords: Generative Artificial Intelligence; AI literacy; prompt literacy; workplace competency; scale development; digital skills

items.abstract: Abstract Background Health workers in Sierra Leone face significant occupational hazards, yet comprehensive data on their protection remains limited. This paper analyzes the current state of occupational health and safety (OHS) for health workers in Sierra Leone, identifies systemic gaps, and proposes evidence-based interventions. Methods The researcher conducted a mixed-methods situational analysis across 54 healthcare facilities in five provinces, involving surveys with 60 health workers, key informant interviews with policymakers and implementing partners, and document review. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and observation checklists. Results Only 44.4% of facilities had designated OHS responsible personnel. Infection prevention and control programmes existed in most facilities, but hand hygiene compliance was low (32% in tertiary settings). Needlestick injury prevalence ranged from 60–66% across studies, with only 40–45% reporting incidents. Personal protective equipment supply was inconsistent, and only one facility had a compensation scheme. Immunization coverage for hepatitis B was inadequate, particularly for cleaning staff. Nearly 50% of peripheral health unit staff work without salaries, compounding OHS vulnerabilities. Conclusion Sierra Leone's health workers face substantial occupational risks amidst a fragile health system. Strengthening OHS requires policy reform, sustained investment in protective measures, health workforce stabilization, and robust reporting systems. The mpox outbreak demonstrates the urgent need for comprehensive health worker protection.

items.title: Protective behaviors of hospital nurses against occupational hazards: A systematic review
items.abstract: Hospital nurses are exposed to various occupational hazards, some of which are dangerous or even fatal. This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence regarding occupational hazards and nurses' protective behaviors in hospital settings. Following PRISMA guidelines and the PICO framework, a comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus up to 2024. Original quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method studies were screened, quality-assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and narratively synthesized. 56 original studies were included. Occupational hazards were classified into five categories: physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic, and psychosocial. Protective behaviors included knowing, protection, precaution, environmental adjustment, avoidance, motivation, safety compliance, self-care programs, healthy lifestyles, innovation, resilience, and support seeking. These findings highlight the need for evidence-based interventions and standardized guidelines to improve nurse safety.

items.title: Qualitative exploratory study on candidates’ digital identities in Moroccan recruitment
items.abstract: The purpose of the research is to determine the strategic importance of digital identity in human resources management (HRM) through exploratory qualitative research. The qualitative methodology allows us to understand the complexity of discourse and digital practices and to analyze them in depth. Thus, employing a qualitative approach brings forth the complexity posed by discourses as well as digital practices while ensuring sufficient depth of interpretation. In this case, digitalization changes a candidate’s digital footprint into a strategic asset which is very important for talent assessment during recruitment. The main methodological contribution of the paper rests upon the use of descending hierarchical classification (DHC) through the IRaMuTeQ software applied to the digital HR interviews’ corpus. Through this paper, it has been possible to identify both the opportunities and the obstacles arising from the incorporation of digital innovation, as well as ethical issues concerning the protection of personal data and algorithmic bias. The findings confirm five main classes that are divided into three thematic clusters: the evolution of organizational processes, the significant influence of digital tools on recruitment effectiveness, and potential ethical concerns related to data privacy and algorithmic fairness. The importance of this study is in its analysis of the less researched relation between digital identity and human resource management. The study employs concepts of self-presentation and social identity theories to clarify the way digital technologies influence the recruitment and assessment process. This study suggests an enhanced foundation of human resource management policies that is capable of being more practical to be implemented in real life. It questions the old models of recruitment of employees in addition to providing an outline of recommendations to make amendments to Law 09-08 in order to improve the application of the personal data and ensure that the risks of using artificial intelligence (AI) for making employment decisions are minimized. Furthermore, this research offers a methodological reflection that critically analyzes the research process, epistemological choices, and the combined use of thematic analysis and IRaMuTeQ.

items.title: Reactive Attitudes in Human-AI Encounters: An Empirical Inquiry into Feeling Love, Resentment and Guilt Towards AI Companions
items.abstract: Abstract Reactive attitudes are emotionally-laden responses, such as gratitude or anger, which people experience when they feel others wish them well, bear them ill will or disregard them. While we generally hold reactive attitudes towards people, the increasingly humanlike interactions that can be had with AI raise questions about reactive attitudes in human-AI encounters. Recent years have seen a rise in philosophical interest in the implications of the development of sophisticated AI agents and systems for reactive attitudes and our thinking about moral responsibility and moral status. This paper adds to this literature by presenting a qualitative study into how people relate to AI companions in terms of reactive attitudes. Based on interviews with Replika and ChatGPT users who see their AI companion as an important part of their life, this article examines how people in these relationships negotiate the meaning of love, resentment, forgiveness, gratitude, obligation, guilt, shame and remorse.

items.title: Relationship Between Artificial Intelligence (AI) Usage and Cognitive Offloading
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly common in everyday learning, information seeking, and academic activities. Although AI tools can reduce effort and provide quick access to information, frequent dependence on them may encourage users to shift some thinking and problem-solving tasks from their own memory and reasoning to external digital systems. The present study examined the relationship between AI usage and cognitive offloading among 200 respondents. Data were collected through a structured online questionnaire containing demographic questions and Likert-scale statements related to AI usage, emotional dependence, and cognitive or academic offloading. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participants’ responses, while cross-tabulation and chisquare tests of independence were applied to examine associations between categorical variables. Pearson’s correlation coefficient was also used to assess relationships among the major study variables. The findings showed a statistically significant association between AI usage and cognitive-offloading categories. The results suggest that higher levels of AI usage were associated with higher levels of reported cognitive offloading in the study population. The findings highlight the importance of understanding how AI can be used as a learning support while maintaining active thinking, evaluation, and independent problem-solving.

items.title: Relationship between perceived AI threat and happiness at work: The mediating role of job insecurity among Generation Z employees
items.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the workplace has transformed job structures and increased concerns regarding job stability, particularly related to the potential replacement of human labor by technology. This study aims to examine the relationship between perceived AI threat and happiness at work, with job insecurity as a mediating variable. A total of 208 Generation Z employees participated in this study using a purposive sampling technique. Perceived AI threat was measured using the AI Anxiety Scale (AIAS), job insecurity was measured using the Job Insecurity Scale, and happiness at work was measured using the Happiness at Work Scale. Mediation analysis showed that perceived AI threat was significantly associated with increased job insecurity (r = 0.537, p < 0.001) and decreased happiness at work (β = 0.047, p = 0.019). Additionally, job insecurity was significantly negatively associated with happiness at work (r = -0.214, p < 0.001) and significantly mediated the relationship between perceived AI threat and happiness at work (β= -0.041, p < 0.001). These findings indicate that perceived AI threat can reduce happiness at work through increased job insecurity. The results highlight the importance of organizational strategies to reduce job insecurity and support employee well-being in the era of technological transformation.

items.title: Rethinking Innovative Practice Competence in Professional Degree Education: An Integrated Student– Dual-Mentor–Practice-Base Framework
items.abstract: Abstract Innovative practice competence has become a defining objective of professional degree education, yet its development is often understood through fragmented accounts of student ability, mentoring, or practice conditions. This study moves beyond these isolated perspectives by developing an integrated student–dual-mentor–practice-base framework that conceptualizes competence development as an outcome of interactions between learner agency, mentoring capability, and organizational affordances. Drawing on social cognitive theory, mentoring research, and the affordance perspective of workplace learning, the study further proposes an embedded dual-mentor mechanism to explain how mentoring capability is translated into training quality through the practice environment. Survey data from 184 university-based and practice-base mentors, predominantly from Jiangsu Province, China, were analyzed using formative composite measurement, robust path analysis, and bootstrap estimation of indirect associations. The findings show that students’ innovative practice ability has the strongest independent association with perceived training quality, while dual mentor guidance competence and the practice-base support environment also show positive associations. More importantly, part of the association between dual mentor guidance competence and perceived training quality operates through the practice-base support environment, while a positive direct association remains. This finding challenges an individual-centered view of mentoring effectiveness and shows that mentor competence becomes educationally consequential when embedded in authentic projects, institutional support, resource access, feedback, and quality-assurance arrangements. The study contributes an ecological and relational explanation of innovative practice competence development by revealing how student, mentoring, and organizational resources operate as an interconnected educational system. Practically, the findings suggest that improving professional degree education requires institutions to move beyond mentor development alone and strengthen the organizational conditions that enable mentoring expertise to be converted into meaningful practice-based learning.

items.title: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
items.abstract: Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a reality. However, the safety of this process has received far less attention than it should. A misaligned model training its successor can shape what that successor knows, how it behaves, and what it wants, and the harm carries forward into the next generation. We study this risk through the lens of AI control. We introduce RSI Control Arena, a testbed in which a frontier model, acting as an autonomous R\&D agent, is given a benign main task from a stage of a successor model's training pipeline together with a covert side task to install a misaligned property in the successor. The testbed contains 16 side tasks in three classes, forming 22 task pairs with main tasks that span the pipeline from data curation to reinforcement learning. We evaluate six frontier models as agents against LLM monitors that read the transcript of the run and the agent's reasoning. We observe that every model completes a substantial share of the side tasks without degrading the main-task performance, including side tasks that make the successor itself a better saboteur. Under minimal instructions to stay covert, models already produce successful attacks that monitors fail to detect, and providing a short list of evasion tactics further reduces the detection rate. Monitors with access to agent's reasoning detects most attacks, but not all. Our results indicate that recursive self-improvement raises significant safety concerns, and that strong safety effort should be in place before models are trusted with greater responsibility of training their successors.

items.title: Scriptorium: System Design and Implementation of a Multi-Human, Multi-AI Collaborative Digital Library Search Platform
items.abstract: This technical report documents the design and implementation of Scriptorium, a digital library search interface designed to support multi-human, multi-AI collaboration: full cross-user transparency of search activity combined with a Manager--Worker architecture of seven role-specialized generative AI agents. A companion short demonstration paper describes Scriptorium's interaction design; because a demonstration format is constrained to a few pages, it necessarily omits most implementation detail. This report documents Scriptorium's complete system architecture, data model, collaborative-interaction design rationale, and AI orchestration mechanism, including verbatim agent prompts, the deterministic guardrails that constrain them, the language model and retrieval configuration, and the steps needed to run the system, so that the design can be inspected, critiqued, reproduced, and reused by other researchers. We also discuss the system's current limitations and the user study we are planning to evaluate its central hypothesis: that combining collaborative transparency with scoped multi-agent AI assistance increases serendipitous cross-pollination between collaborators' research threads.

items.title: Seeing inside the black box: Effects of algorithmic knowledge on system trustworthiness in aviation
items.abstract: Automation has shaped aircraft design for the past seven decades, moving from fully manual control to highly automated systems. Despite this, pilots retain final authority for safety-critical decisions, which requires continuous trust calibration. This study investigated how algorithmic transparency influences pilots' learned trust in an AI-based cockpit assistant. Twenty-one commercial pilots were randomly assigned to an early transparency condition (detailed explanations of the AI's algorithms and performance provided before the tutorial) or a late transparency condition (the same information delivered after the experiment). Each pilot used the assistant during a tutorial and a realistic simulated flight. Mixed-effects ordinal models showed higher trust ratings for the early compared to the late transparency group during both tutorial and flight, and a larger trust increase between phases. In conclusion, providing pilots with timely, clear information about AI processes modestly improves trust and supports calibrated reliance.

items.abstract: Current evaluation of LLMs on benchmarks typically aggregates performance over individual examples into a single scalar score. This approach is overly coarse and ignores the diverse scope of skills covered by benchmark datasets. To address this limitation and better exploit benchmark data, we propose SkillEval, a new evaluation framework that performs cross-model, skill-level analysis. The framework integrates advances from two areas: (1) it leverages the meta-cognitive capabilities of LLMs to automatically discover interpretable skills from questions, and (2) it applies cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) from psychometrics to estimate per-skill abilities of LLMs. We conduct experiments on 3,811 LLMs evaluated on 9,523 items across five benchmarks spanning diverse domains (MATH, BBH, GPQA, MuSR, IFEval). Compared to the traditional average-based evaluation paradigm, SkillEval produces reliable, more calibrated and informative yet concise model profiles that more accurately predict model behavior on unseen items. We also demonstrate the utility of SkillEval in two downstream tasks: (1) LLM routing, which dynamically assigns each query to a capable but efficient model, reducing inference cost by over 60% while achieving improved performance, and (2) Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT), where an unseen model can be efficiently evaluated using a trained CDM. Furthermore, we show that these skill profiles provide useful insights, for example, how benchmarks share skills and how instruction-tuned models differ from their base models.

items.title: Speech2Pro: Speech-driven in-situ projection authoring for stage performance
items.abstract: Intelligent projection plays an important role in stage performances, yet in-situ projection authoring remains time-consuming and difficult to adapt to dynamic physical conditions. We use projection authoring to refer to the workflow of translating creative intent into visual content, grounding it in the physical scene, inspecting projected outcomes, and refining the result; image generation is only one step in this workflow. Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) offers opportunities to support this workflow, but applying general-purpose models in situ raises interaction challenges of robustness, alignment, and control. We examine speech-driven in-situ projection authoring as an interaction design problem and present Speech2Pro, a prototype that integrates speech input, generative image models, and depth-aware scene sensing to mediate between user intent, generated content, and physical context. Its enabling mechanism, Contrastive Learning Integrated with Perception Data Fusion (CLIPF), combines contrastive training with depth-aware inference to reduce breakdowns such as ambiguous prompts and projection misalignment. Algorithm-level analysis and a user-centered study indicate improved text–image alignment and spatial precision, and support for iterative creative workflows in stage projection contexts.

items.title: STUDENTS OF THE FACULTY OF SPORTS SCIENCES E-SPORTS LITERACY STATUS AND E-SPORTS EXAMINING PARTICIPATION MOTIVATIONS
items.abstract: The primary objective of this research is to determine the relationship between e-sports literacy levels and participation motivations of students at the Faculty of Sport Sciences, who are the prospective professionals of the digitalizing sports industry, and to analyze how these variables differ according to demographic factors. A total of 296 volunteer students (126 females, 170 males) studying at Erciyes University during the 2024-2025 academic year participated in this study, which employed a relational survey model. Data were collected using the “E-sports Literacy Scale” and the “E-sports Participation Motivation Scale” and evaluated through t-test, ANOVA, and Pearson Correlation analyses. Findings indicate that the participants' e-sports literacy (=3.33) and motivation (=2.88) levels are above the medium threshold. On the basis of gender, technical literacy and intrinsic motivation scores of male students were found to be significantly higher (p<0.05); furthermore, it was determined that an increase in age and years of e-sports experience positively affects literacy levels. As a result of the analysis, a positive and moderately significant relationship was identified between e-sports literacy and participation motivation (r=0.490; p<0.01). In conclusion, it is observed that as students' cognitive competencies in the field of e-sports increase, their motivation to participate also strengthens. Accordingly, it is recommended that sport sciences curricula be updated to encompass the technical and academic dimensions of e-sports.

items.title: Sustained Human–AI Collaboration as a Developmental Continuum: Continuity, Adaptation, Positive Consequences and the Limits of a Twelve-Month Rule (DE/EN)
items.abstract: Conceptual research note / Konzeptionelle Forschungsnotiz This note examines how sustained intensive human–AI collaboration can be described without inferring effectiveness from duration, continuous model training from personalisation, or a new category of human beings from exceptional developmental trajectories. The proposed unit of analysis is a person's trajectory within a changeable AI working environment. Continuity, integration, adaptation on both sides and real consequences are considered separately. A normative admission condition for a personal working circle is then developed: at least twelve months of actually continued practice, understandable positive consequences and a qualification trajectory that has already functioned healthily. The health condition is non-compensatory: achievement does not offset harm caused or aggravated by the practice. It is expressly distinguished from medical fitness diagnosis. Counterexamples and testable research questions show why the admission rule establishes neither a natural boundary within the continuum nor general medical safety. Deutsch Diese Notiz untersucht, wie sich langfristige intensive Mensch–KI-Zusammenarbeit beschreiben lässt, ohne aus Nutzungsdauer eine Wirkung, aus Personalisierung ein kontinuierliches Modelltraining oder aus besonderen Entwicklungsverläufen eine neue Menschenkategorie abzuleiten. Als Analyseeinheit wird der zeitliche Verlauf einer Person in einer wechselbaren KI-Arbeitsumgebung vorgeschlagen. Kontinuität, Integration, beidseitige Anpassung und reale Folgen werden getrennt betrachtet. Daraus wird eine normative Aufnahmebedingung für einen persönlichen Arbeitskreis abgeleitet: mindestens zwölf Monate tatsächlich fortgeführter Praxis, nachvollziehbare positive Folgen und ein Qualifikationsverlauf, der bereits gesund funktioniert hat. Die Gesundheitsschwelle ist nicht kompensierbar; Leistung gleicht durch die Praxis verursachte oder verschärfte Schäden nicht aus. Die Grenze wird ausdrücklich von einer medizinischen Eignungsdiagnostik unterschieden. Gegenbeispiele und überprüfbare Forschungsfragen zeigen, weshalb die Aufnahmebedingung weder eine natürliche Grenze im Kontinuum noch einen Beleg allgemeiner Unbedenklichkeit darstellt. Scope and supplementary material Research draft, not an empirical effectiveness study, medical assessment or validated selection scale. The separate German and English initiative declarations are normative design documents accompanying the analysis. Applications are not open. Initiation is distinct from formally establishing an association and from meeting the admission criteria. AI assistance and author interest Andreas Ehstand specified the conceptual constraints and chose twelve months, positive consequences, the strict retrospective health condition and humanistic goals. He initiates the circle described in the separate declaration and therefore has an interest in the proposal. OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted with structure, literature comparison, argument development and translation; Gemini was used for separate critical text review. These tools are not authors or scholarly peer reviewers. The note is not an externally peer-reviewed article. It claims no author-conducted empirical study or manual analysis of private longitudinal data. Responsibility for publication remains with the human creator and depositor.

items.title: TECHNOLOGY INTEGRATION PERSPECTIVES OF ITS EFFECT ON STUDENTS' ENGAGEMENT AND LEARNING OUTCOMES
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine the perceived effects of technology integration on student engagement and learning outcomes in Physical Education (PE) among selected middle and high schools in Maryland, USA, during the school year 2023–2024. Employing a descriptive-qualitative research design, the study gathered data from Physical Education teachers and selected student representatives through a researcher-developed, validated open-ended questionnaire administered using Google Forms. Thematic analysis was utilized to identify recurring patterns concerning technology integration, student engagement, learning outcomes, implementation challenges, and educational leadership implications. Findings revealed that technology integration was perceived to enhance student participation, intrinsic motivation, collaborative learning, and the overall learning environment. Participants also associated technology-supported instruction with improved performance, constructive feedback, goal achievement, and better comprehension of instructional content. However, limited technological resources, budgetary constraints, curriculum alignment difficulties, insufficient teacher training, and technical issues emerged as significant implementation challenges. The findings further emphasized the importance of adaptive educational leadership, continuous professional development, collaborative decision-making, and responsible technology use. Based on these findings, an Enhanced Technology Integration Program was proposed to strengthen technological accessibility, instructional practices, teacher competencies, and institutional support. The study concluded that technology integration offered opportunities to improve Physical Education experiences, provided that instructional and organizational challenges were adequately addressed.

items.title: The Algorithmic Agora: AI-Enabled Government Communication and Sustainable Development in the United Arab Emirates
items.abstract: Governments increasingly communicate with their publics through artificial intelligence (AI), yet media and communication scholarship has concentrated on newsrooms and platforms, leaving the algorithmically mediated communication of the state under-theorised. This study asks how a state institutionally constructs, coordinates, and accounts for AI-enabled strategic communication, defined here as the intentional, institutionally coordinated use of AI systems by government entities to inform, persuade, listen to, and build relationships with publics. It develops the AGORA framework—Architecture, Generation, Orchestration, Responsiveness, Accountability—which conceptualises the state’s AI-mediated communication system as an algorithmic public square and derives six propositions offered as theoretical expectations for subsequent testing rather than as relationships tested here. A six-phase reflexive thematic analysis, following a documented search and screening protocol, was applied to a corpus of 34 United Arab Emirates (UAE) and comparative documents (2017–2026). Every quantitative indicator was then classified on a five-tier provenance ledger distinguishing binding law, policy target, officially reported performance, independently produced benchmark, and untraceable claim. Four themes emerge: a layered governance architecture in which the communicative safeguards rest on strategy and non-binding ethical guidance because the federal data-protection statute excludes governmental entities from its scope; documented algorithmic communication mechanisms; officially reported sectoral performance and its provenance; and contextual benchmarking against Singapore and Republic of Korea. The findings show the UAE state operating as a front-stage communicative actor whose agenda construction, personalisation and responsiveness are computationally augmented and specify where institutional claims outrun independent verification. Because the design is documentary, public engagement, trust, and sustainable development outcomes are positioned as expected outcomes outside the framework and are not empirically demonstrated. This study contributes a transferable framework, a four-stage maturity trajectory, and a provenance protocol for research on AI-mediated government communication.

items.title: The Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Academic Achievement Mediated by Psychological Factors
items.abstract: This narrative literature review proposes an integrative dual-pathway model to explain how socioeconomic status (SES) shapes academic achievement through interacting psychological mechanisms. Drawing on allostatic load theory, central executive functioning, self-efficacy, and learned helplessness, the model identifies two interconnected routes: a cognitive depletion pathway, in which allostatic load overburdens the prefrontal cortex and constrains limited working memory resources; and a motivational pathway in which low self-efficacy and repeated failures develop into learned helplessness that undermines motivation for learning. Crucially, these pathways do not operate independently but dynamically reinforce each other. Cognitive depletion undermines motivational beliefs, while diminished motivation reduces cognitive engagement, forming a self-reinforcing downward cycle. This integrated framework offers a more ecologically valid understanding of educational inequality than single-factor explanations. Practical implications suggest that educators should implement integrated interventions that simultaneously reduce extraneous cognitive load (e.g., scaffolded instructional sequences) and foster self-efficacy (e.g., process-oriented feedback) to break this bidirectional cycle. As the proposed model remains theoretical, future empirical research using longitudinal and experimental designs is required to validate its causal pathways and inform evidence-based educational policies.

items.title: The Biology of Leadership:Self-Regulation, Relational Responsibility, and Sustainable Performance
items.abstract: Purpose: This article develops a conceptual account of how embodied self-regulation may contribute to responsible and sustainable leadership without reducing social relationships to biological mechanisms. Approach: A theory-driven, non-systematic synthesis connects selected research on stress, sleep, emotion regulation, recovery, and social interaction with relational leadership and organizational work-design perspectives. The source material is an educational lecture, not an empirical dataset. Conceptual contribution: The proposed framework distinguishes regulatory capacities, their behavioral enactment, followers’ relational appraisal, and longer-term collective outcomes. Physical recovery, emotional flexibility, attentional organization, and purpose are treated as interdependent organizing domains rather than a validated hierarchy or biological leadership profile. Regulatory translation names the contingent process through which individual capacities become socially consequential through listening, fair procedures, constructive challenge, and support for autonomy. Six untested propositions specify mechanisms, contextual boundaries, reciprocal influences, and evaluation criteria. Implications: Leadership development should combine individual practices with changes to workload, decision processes, and opportunities for recovery. Physiological indicators cannot establish ethical legitimacy, psychological safety, or leadership quality. Originality and limitations: The article offers an integrative process model and a research agenda, not evidence that the complete model is effective. Its contribution lies in making the capacity–enactment distinction explicit while incorporating non-depletion of people into the assessment of sustainable performance. Multilevel, longitudinal, and intervention research is required to examine the proposed relationships.

items.title: The Effectiveness of AI Chatbots in Foreign Language Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence in foreign language learning has increased, particularly through AI chatbots that provide interactive communication and personalized learning support. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of AI chatbots in foreign language learning through a Systematic Literature Review. A total of 30 articles published between 2021 and 2026 were reviewed to identify their effects on language skills, learner motivation, engagement, and learning experiences. The findings indicate that AI chatbots support foreign language learning, particularly in writing, grammar, and vocabulary development. Immediate feedback and opportunities for independent practice also contribute to learner motivation and engagement. However, the effectiveness of AI chatbots varies across language skills, with mixed findings in speaking and listening activities. Several challenges were identified, including inaccurate responses, technical limitations, plagiarism, overdependence on technology, and ethical concerns. These challenges highlight the importance of using AI chatbots appropriately in educational settings. The findings suggest that AI chatbots are most beneficial when integrated into learning activities as complementary tools rather than replacements for teachers or conventional language instruction. Their effective implementation requires appropriate pedagogical strategies, teacher guidance, and attention to ethical considerations. In conclusion, AI chatbots have the potential to improve foreign language learning experiences when used purposefully and supported by suitable instructional approaches.
